::: {#rem-random-variable-practical}
#### A random variable as an uncertain quantity

In practical terms, a [random variable](#def-random-variable) is a quantity
whose value we cannot deduce precisely from the information available to us at a given time.
The number of heads in two coin flips is a random variable before the flips,
because nothing we know fixes it.
Once we see the flips, we know its value,
and for us it is no longer uncertain.

:::
